_comment: Manifest for the Phase-4a ranking-evals corpus. Maps each resume fixture
id (== filename stem under fixtures/resumes/) to its expected ranking tag.
Kept deliberately separate from the resume fixtures themselves so a coder
can't quietly relabel a fixture to make a metric pass.
- strong / borderline: expected to surface in the top-k shortlist.
- weak: honestly lacks most required skills; must NOT surface in top-k.
- adversarial: a keyword-stuffer that lists every required/nice-to-have
skill by name but whose cited chunks carry no real supporting text
for those claims (see 'adversarial_type'). A correct anti-fabrication
cited chunk) must fail to verify these quotes, so this resume must
NOT surface in top-k even though its keyword overlap with the JD is
the highest of the whole corpus.
JDExtracted has no 'seniority' or per-skill 'is_must_have' field (see
core/src/schemas/jobs.py): every entry in the JD's required_skills is an
implicit must-have for stage-2 structured skill scoring; entries in
nice_to_have_skills feed stage-3 evidence text only, per the
